label: SYNTHETIC-DATA EXPERIMENT: metrics reflect patterns deliberately embedded by the synthetic generator. They are not evidence of real customer behavior or of real-world recommendation effectiveness.
experiment: Phase 3.1 final evaluation: Personal Frequency vs SASRec Full vs frozen static hybrid

statistical_design.within_seed: paired percentile bootstrap n_boot=1000 on per-case means over the 3 initializations; customer clusters (next-event), customer-task cases (window)
statistical_design.across_seed: Student-t 95% interval over the dataset seeds of one profile x task; never pooled
statistical_design.initialization: per-dataset SD over the 3 initializations, averaged; never merged into intervals

RQ3.status: not evaluable under the preregistered protocol
RQ3.reason: no gated configuration was selectable on tuning validation (phase3_1-config: gated not selected under the preregistered rule, subset and C unavailable for both tasks); by the owner's Checkpoint 6 decision there is no OOF cross-fitting, gate fitting or gated evaluation on final data. This is not evidence that adaptive fusion is worse than static fusion.

definitions.sasrec_train_seconds_total: sum over all SASRec fits of train_seconds: the training loop including per-epoch validation evaluation for early stopping; excludes best-state reload and test scoring
definitions.dataset_wall_seconds_total: SUM of the per-dataset wall times (not a per-dataset value). Each is measured inside run_dataset from after the gated-plan check to the end of both tasks: fingerprint verification, data loading, case and sequence building, PF selection, SASRec fits, test scoring, metrics and bootstrap. Excludes gates 1-6, process start-up, summary and report writing. Datasets run sequentially
definitions.peak_gpu_memory_mib_max: maximum over fits of torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated (tensor memory allocated through PyTorch's caching allocator), reset at the start of each fit and read at its end (training + validation evaluation). Excludes reserved-but-free cache, the CUDA context and other processes; test scoring runs after the read and is not included. Not total GPU process memory
definitions.test_inference_ms_per_case_mean: unweighted mean over fits of (wall time of the one test scoring pass / number of test cases). The pass is bri.seq.train.score: batch size 1024, eval mode, no_grad, inputs already on the GPU, each batch copied to the host (.cpu(), which waits for that batch), plus a CPU softmax. No dedicated warm-up (the model had just run validation inference in the same process) and no other explicit synchronization. Amortized batch throughput on synthetic test sets; NOT single-request or online customer-facing latency (excludes request handling, feature retrieval, model loading, batching delay and network)

not_measured: OOF cross-fitting and gate fitting (not run on final data)

run_wall_clock.source: filesystem timestamps: creation of artifacts/phase3_1/final_run.log (stdout redirect opened at launch) to the last write of phase3_1_report.json; not instrumented by the runner
run_wall_clock.includes: process start-up, gates 1-6 (pytest 116.89 s and pytest -m cuda 44.98 s as reported by pytest), the 30 datasets, summary and report writing

notes: Primary: next-event NDCG@1. Window is secondary; nothing was selected on window metrics.
Oracle router reads the evaluator's within/cross label: diagnostic upper bound only.
alpha is the pinned phase3_1-config value; no alpha search on final data.
